acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on time and headcount. Cloud usually costs less to start and more as people and data grow, especially when priced per seat. On-premise adds hardware and an installation up front, then a flat cost. Compare the total over three to five years at your expected team size, not the first invoice.

mainEntity.name: Is cloud welding software less secure?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not automatically. A well-run cloud service can be very secure, but it is reachable on the public internet by design. An on-premise system can stay off the public internet entirely — if remote access is built without open ports. Ask either kind of vendor how access is secured.

mainEntity.name: Can on-premise software be reached from outside the shop?

acceptedAnswer.text: It can, if the vendor provides a secure way in, such as an encrypted overlay network. Be wary of solutions that rely on open ports or a VPN you have to run yourself.

mainEntity.name: Do I need IT staff to run on-premise software?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not if the vendor manages it: they install, update and repair the appliance remotely, and your part is keeping it powered. With classic self-hosted software, you do.

mainEntity.name: Can I start in the cloud and move on-premise later?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ask the vendor how records move between the two before you commit. With our products, Atlas customers can move their WPS library and welder qualifications into Elenchon at launch.
